title: Step from a tape movement action
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Turing machine and $c$ a configuration. Suppose $c$ has state $q$, and the transition of $M$ at $q$ on the symbols currently read is the action that moves the input head by $\mathrm{inp}$, moves tape $i$ by $m$, makes no writes or output, and enters state $q'$. Then the next configuration has state $q'$, input-head position obtained by moving $c$'s input head by $\mathrm{inp}$ with boundary clamping, and work-head positions equal to those of $c$ except that tape $i$'s position is increased by $m$; all other components are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: the transition at $q$ on the currently read symbols is the specified tape action
